Perhaps siliconlottery, just ran a Heaven Benchmark on Ultra settings 1440p with gsync enabled, maxed out at 68C with fans on auto and yet only got to 50% speed.
The settings I use in GPUTweak are +192 core, max voltage, +490 on memory (didn't feel like stressing it) and powertarget of 109% which should theoretically max out at 87C but doesn't no matter what game I run. While gaming I rarely hit over 64C and fans have never to my knowledge ever gone past 50% threshold. 
The only gripe I have is that in GPUTweak it shows that boostclock should be at 1925 but it doesn't, it goes to 2101 ingame and in benchmarks.

comments.text:
You have a point with the network card, and I agree manufacturers should include drivers with it. But this is very different from the drivers of your graphics card.

Graphics card drivers get constantly updated with various improvements, even optimization for new games(so called game ready drivers), so what is the point of buying a top tier graphics card without getting the newest drivers? You should ALWAYS get the newest drivers anyways, hence rendering the old drivers included pointless.

The manufacturer's mind set is probably "oh ppl probably want the card to 'work' right out of the box or they'll blame not knowing how to install the drivers correctly on me so i should probably include an old stable version of the driver so it always works even if it is old and slow but ppl who understand download the newest ones anyways so I always win duh"

I would go as far as to say this is detrimental to the consumers, because they really don't get the full performance out of their hard earned cash.

Steam installs all the required stuff for you when you first start a game(e.g. DirectX, VC++). Manually installing DirectX is really an old memory from a long time ago...

Additional softwares on the installation disk aren't all so esoteric, and you probably want to find newer versions or better versions online somewhere. But seriously I can't think of any really useful game related software other than maybe fraps(fps counter) and Afterburner(overclocking)...software that manages the LED lights?
